items.title: George P. Fleming Interview, 1984-10-06
items.q: Like I remember like during that time Fletcher Henderson was arranging for Paul Whiteman.

ctx.x: You said they had sheet music, you know, all those bands that we hear now, you know, they made these records in the late, in the 60s, the late 50s, 60s, 70s, the kind of preservation hall bands. Were they playing the same kind of music then or was it much more arranged?

Well, before then they were playing more traditional jazz and the sheet music brought a lot of modern playing in. Like I remember like during that time Fletcher Henderson was arranging for Paul Whiteman. Yeah, it was Fletcher Henderson and a guy by the name of Don Redmond made a lot of Paul Whiteman's arrangements and Fletcher Henderson rather was arranging for Benny Goodman and then they had the music started, we started, I would start it rather playing sheet music like they had one of the pieces I remember was…
